title: Tunity
slugLine: A blockchain-backed music rights and AI-licensing platform that pays artists every time AI uses their music.

role.title: Product Manager @ Tunity.
moves: Generated a PRD to facilitate handoff to design team, and **guided creation of a compliant product prototype**
Conducted 2 expert interviews to determine product scope and direction, **identified 5 leads for sales and marketing partnership**
Created pitch deck and visual value proposition for Tunity., **yielding a successful presentation**

research.problem: ==Independent music creators== are having their music **==scraped to train AI models==** without consent or pay, and there is no way to trace AI-generated music back to its original source.

stakeholders.name: AI companies
stakeholders.note: Model builders and music AI apps

painPoints.label: Lost income
painPoints.detail: AI models that generate music undercut human creators, causing them to lose income from commissions and licensing. Even though their music has probably been used to train these models, they have no way of being compensated for its use.

painPoints.label: AI slop saturation
painPoints.detail: Mass produced AI generated content quickly floods platforms and drowns out real creators. When AI music dominates the platform it makes future AI training more difficult.

painPoints.label: Limited creator rights
painPoints.detail: Creators have little control over whether their work is scraped or used for AI training.

painPoints.label: Lost provenance
painPoints.detail: Authorship and ownership become difficult to trace after content is copied, modified, or processed by AI, making monetization difficult.

painPoints.label: Fragmented protection
painPoints.detail: Existing solutions are often platform-specific and do not give individual creators persistent, cross-platform control.

insights.insight: Most tools that pay creators run through label deals
insights.evidence: The competitive map splits the field two ways: defend or monetize, and built for independent creators or for labels. Sureel, Musical AI and the Udio and Suno deals all sit on the label side.

insights.insight: Defending a catalog is not the same as earning from it
insights.evidence: ArtyShield is built for independent musicians, but in the comparison it neither licenses to AI nor pays creators.

insights.insight: Regulation gives AI companies a reason to buy
insights.evidence: The EU AI Act requires AI providers to publish training-data summaries and keep a copyright policy. A rights-cleared catalog gives them that proof under one license, not thousands.

insights.insight: The majors are buying up attribution
insights.evidence: WMG bought Sureel in June 2026 and Sony backs Vermillio. Tunity works with any distributor and keeps creators, not labels, in control.

design.lead: Musicians register tracks and stems as tamper-proof proof of ownership, choose how AI may use each work, and license it to AI companies through a rights-cleared marketplace that pays them automatically for every training or sampling use.

items.title: Register
items.body: Audio fingerprint + on-chain timestamp-verify registration & provenance

items.title: Set terms
items.body: Per track or stem: no AI, license for training, or sample with credit

items.title: License
items.body: AI companies license a rights-cleared catalog via smart contracts

items.title: Get paid
items.body: Automatic royalties, usage dashboard and misuse alerts

blocks.title: Market sizing

rings.name: TAM
rings.label: Total addressable market
rings.note: AI compensation owed to music creators: €12.59B global music royalties × ~25% at risk from AI (CISAC: 24%) ≈ €3.1B (≈ $3.5B). Our 20% take: ≈ $700M.

rings.name: SAM
rings.label: Serviceable addressable market
rings.note: US performance royalties reachable via PROs: ASCAP $1.95B + BMI ~$1.57B ≈ $3.5B × 25% at risk. Our 20% take: ≈ $176M.

rings.name: SOM
rings.label: Serviceable obtainable market
rings.note: One PRO partnership (ASCAP): 5–10% of its AI-licensing flow ($1.95B × 25%) within 3–5 years. Our 20% take: ≈ $5–10M.

blocks.note: Sources: CISAC Global Collections Report 2025; CISAC AI study, Dec 2024; ASCAP 2025 revenue, Music Business Worldwide, Feb 2026; BMI FY2022 revenue, PR Newswire.
